PARTNER INTERPRETATION NOTE

TPTN is a Canada-first sovereign digital trade infrastructure initiative — not a SaaS platform, marketplace, or venture-backed product. The prototype shown in this briefing demonstrates a structured, auditable, standards-aligned digital workflow for a single Canadian SME export transaction, observable by authorized commercial and government-side participants without claiming live regulatory integration.

The architecture is designed to help make Canada’s existing trade agreements operationally usable by SME exporters — structuring records once to international standards and allowing authorized exporters, buyers, logistics providers, customs brokers, and government-side reviewers to work from the same auditable transaction record.

Current stage: Clickable demonstrator using synthetic data. MVP build and pilot-planning discussions are underway. No production deployment, no live government integration, and no executed pilot are implied.

Purpose of this briefing: To provide PwC partners with a concise internal reference showing how the TPTN demonstrator structures a Canadian SME export transaction, connects authorized participant views, and preserves auditability, standards alignment, and scope discipline.

What this briefing does not imply: Procurement, endorsement, validation, funding commitment, or any commitment from PwC or any public-sector party.

AI Governance · Document Preparation · Inline Decision Support
Order Management & AI Trade Agent — Inline Advisory in Context
Exporters Module
Orders & Documentation tab · AI Trade Agent panel
What this shows
AI Trade Agent screens showing the intended interaction discipline: reasoning displayed with each suggestion, uncertainty explicitly flagged on fields requiring exporter input rather than left silent, all AI-prepared content presented for exporter confirmation before submission, and the explicit statement that the AI Trade Agent does not submit documents on the exporter's behalf. Inline Q&A: exporter asks why ORD-2026-PR-0221 was flagged — AI provides the eBL endorsement basis, what action is required, and the estimated resolution time. Second query: verified buyer signals for HS 1106.20 — AI returns two matched buyers with declared import interest, volume range, and corridor status. The Activity Log captures each AI action — including flagged exceptions — for audit.
Institutional signal
The interaction pattern is designed around advisory support with human confirmation at each consequential step — the AI surfaces, reasons, and prepares; the exporter confirms and authorises. Uncertainty is not silent — it is surfaced, logged, and directed to the exporter for review. This is the design intent for AI governance within the platform, aligned with the direction of Canadian federal AI governance expectations including the Directive on Automated Decision-Making and emerging Treasury Board guidance on the use of AI in regulated decision-making contexts.

What this shows
Four active assurance items: Regulatory Conflict (controlled substance HS 2905, escalation to Senior Officer), Incomplete Document Set (2 of 7 documents, human authorisation required), Phytosanitary Certificate Confirmation (CFIA-scope, sign-off required before handoff), Pending eBL Endorsement (MLETR-aligned, carrier endorsement in progress). Institutional signal
The Assurance Mandate is unambiguous: "no shipment with a regulatory exception, compliance conflict, or data integrity concern may advance beyond the pre-handoff gate without explicit human review and authorisation. This function is a designed assurance control, not a workflow fallback." Automated systems surface and flag; humans authorise and release. This is the HITL architecture that addresses federal AI governance expectations at the points where regulatory exceptions arise.

Governance Framework · Standards Alignment · Audit Trail
Standards Alignment, Audit Trail & Record Traceability
Government Oversight View
Governance & Audit tab
What this shows
Four standards cards: MLETR (UNCITRAL/UNIDROIT — Legal Reliability — electronic transferable records, legal equivalence with paper), UN/CEFACT (UN Economic Commission for Europe — Interoperable Exchange — standardised trade document schemas), WCO Data Model (World Customs Organization — Audit-Ready Governance — cross-border data harmonisation, Single Window submission), CAN/DGSI 104 (Digital Governance Council of Canada — Digital Governance — Canadian standard for digital governance in trade and public sector). Below: Illustrative Audit Trail with integrity hashes per event.
Institutional signal
Each standard is attributed to its governing body and framed by function — not listed as credentials but explained as design stance with operational consequence. The CAN/DGSI 104 entry is particularly relevant for federal reviewers: "supports TPTN's position as domestically governed Canadian digital trade infrastructure." The Illustrative Audit Trail with simulated integrity hashes closes the deck on the evidentiary architecture — in production, all record events would be cryptographically signed and immutably logged.

Internal Evaluation Focus
What the prototype demonstrates

The TPTN demonstrator shows how a Canadian SME export transaction can be structured once, governed through an auditable transaction record, and made visible to authorized commercial and government-side participants without claiming live regulatory integration. The value demonstrated is not a standalone interface; it is the operating model for standards-aligned, compliance-grade trade execution.

What deeper assessment should test
  • Adoption pathway: What institutional, commercial, and public-sector conditions would be required for a defined-scope pilot?
  • Business case: Which transaction types, corridors, and stakeholder groups provide the clearest near-term validation pathway?
  • Governance and operating model: What controls, legal agreements, data-residency requirements, and partner roles would need to be confirmed before pilot execution?
This briefing is provided for internal evaluation only and does not imply procurement, endorsement, validation, funding commitment, or commitment from PwC or any public-sector party.
